fact: Bedzrah said persons enrolling in the National Service Scheme must undergo NIA verification and are verified again before payments are made.
Republic Online reports that GRA revenue collection and NHIS member verification depend on NIA biometric verification, with GRA owing $377 million and NHIS $58 million for it.

The National Identification Authority says the civil service payroll (the Mechanized Payroll System) now requires the Ghana Card PIN to validate recruited public sector employees and pensioners, with existing staff to submit their PIN at NIA offices, launched 10 January 2024.
The NIA Executive Secretary says the Ghana Card already serves as the Taxpayer Identification Number, SSNIT and NHIS numbers.
Minister Muntaka said NIA registration enabled integration with the Ghana Revenue Authority, the National Health Insurance Scheme and SSNIT.

Citi Newsroom reports the government payroll platform is integrated with the National Identification Authority database and payroll entries are keyed on NIA numbers, with employees logging on using them, per the Controller and Accountant-General's memo of 11 February 2026.
Mahamudu Bawumia says the government payroll was checked against the Ghana Card, starting with SSNIT and then the National Service Scheme.
Mahamudu Bawumia says Ghana Card checks removed 29,000 ghost names at SSNIT (saving GH¢400 million) and 44,000 at the National Service Scheme (over GH¢300 million); these are his own figures.
The Ghana National Household Registry's July 2026 privacy policy says it collects each registrant's NIA Ghana Card number, so the national ID number is a field of the public household registry.
Dr Benjamin Quaye of the Lands Commission says the Commission is integrating the Ghana Card into its land system for identity-based transactions.
